messages.subject: scale_colour_grey and name
parts:
Dear list members,

I am trying to use scale_colour_grey, but igot an error:

> p = ggplot(geo, aes(x, y, size = md, colour = md))
> p + geom_point() + theme_bw() + facet_wrap(~sitio, scales="free") + scale_size(name = "Indice", breaks = c(0.1, 0.5, 1, 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 50)) + scale_colour_grey(name = "Indice", start = 0.1, end = 0.9, breaks = c(0.1, 0.5, 1, 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 50))+ xlab("Longitud") + ylab("Latitud") + opts(axis.text.x = theme_text(size = 8, vjust = 1)) + opts(axis.text.y = theme_text(size = 8, hjust = 1))
Error: Continuous variable (Indice) supplied to discrete scale_grey.

Does anybody know why?
Best,

Manuel

Another option would be to use a continuous color scale, and set the
high and low values to different shades of grey, like this

p = ggplot(geo, aes(x, y, size = md, colour = md))
p + geom_point() + theme_bw() + facet_wrap(~sitio, scales="free") +
scale_size(name = "Indice", breaks = c(0.1, 0.5, 1, 5, 10, 15, 20, 25,

50)) + scale_colour_gradient(name = "Indice", low = "#000000", high =
"#D3D3D3", breaks = c(0.1, 0.5, 1, 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 50))+

xlab("Longitud") + ylab("Latitud") + opts(axis.text.x =
theme_text(size = 8, vjust = 1)) + opts(axis.text.y = theme_text(size
= 8, hjust = 1))

messages.subject: Re: scale_colour_grey and name
parts:
I just came across this while trying to do a similar problem, searched
the boards and found this post so I'll reply to it.

The issue here is that scale_grey works on a sequential (discrete)
scale as opposed to a continuous one. So when it gets a continuous
variable, it errors just like scale_shape would. (Which turns out to
be a bad example because, in a bizarre turn of events, scale_shape
works with continuous variables. Try running qplot(1:10, 1:10, shape
= rnorm(10)) .) I always thought that the grey scale was a kind of
simplified wrapper for scale_gradient(low = 'black', high = 'white');
is there a reason why it forces a discrete scale?

My feeling after this little investigation - http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4DVAsmrwdtQ

Cheers
david.

parts:
> The issue here is that scale_grey works on a sequential (discrete)
> scale as opposed to a continuous one.  So when it gets a continuous
> variable, it errors just like scale_shape would. (Which turns out to
> be a bad example because, in a bizarre turn of events, scale_shape
> works with continuous variables.  Try running qplot(1:10, 1:10, shape
> = rnorm(10)) .)
Yes, this is a long-standing bug that I need to fix :(

> I always thought that the grey scale was a kind of
> simplified wrapper for scale_gradient(low = 'black', high = 'white');
> is there a reason why it forces a discrete scale?

Because it's not a short cut for scale_gradient - it's a more like a
specialised version of gradient for discrete variables (when they are
actually ordered)
